column1: # derivation: DISTINCT f over sort_rows, then COUNT(*) AS n and COUNT(f)
# AS nf with no grouping key. f = 1.5, 0.0, -0.0, -2.5, NULL, 0.0, 0.5.
# §2.6: as a DISTINCT key -0.0 equals 0.0, so the three zeros are one value;
# §2.4: the one NULL is one row. Distinct rows: 1.5, a zero, -2.5, NULL, 0.5:
# n = 5. COUNT(f) skips the NULL (§2.1): nf = 4. Seven rows less the two
# repeated zeros is 5 again. A scalar aggregate gives one row (§2.3). Which
# zero represents the group is not part of the result (§2.6), so the case
# counts rather than lists. Types: INT64, never NULL (§8.6).
